title: Chemical Energetics - Identifying Energy Changes
topic: Chemical Energetics - Endothermic and Exothermic Reactions
subject: Chemistry

questions.question:
A student mixes solutions of sodium hydroxide and hydrochloric acid. The thermometer reading increases from 25°C to 35°C during the reaction.

Which statement correctly describes this reaction?
options: Energy was absorbed from the surroundings causing cooling
Energy was transferred to the surroundings causing heating
No energy change occurred because mass was conserved
Energy remained trapped inside the solution
questions.explanation: Temperature increase indicates energy transfer to surroundings = Exothermic reaction. Heat is released from system into the solution/environment.

questions.question:
Ammonium nitrate crystals are dissolved in water. The beaker feels cold and the temperature drops from 25°C to 18°C.

What type of process is dissolving ammonium nitrate in water?
options: Exothermic because crystals break down into smaller pieces
Endothermic because energy is absorbed from surroundings
Exothermic because ions form in solution releasing heat
Endothermic because water molecules lose kinetic energy spontaneously
questions.explanation: Temperature drop means heat has left the surroundings and entered the system. Endothermic processes take in energy, causing cooling effect.

questions.question:
Combustion of methane gas releases a large amount of heat:

CH₄(g) + 2O₂(g) → CO₂(g) + 2H₂O(l)

Which classification BEST fits this reaction type?
options: Endothermic because oxygen combines with carbon
Exothermic because energy is released to surroundings
Neutral because no temperature change occurs
Isothermic because both reactants and products have similar energy
questions.explanation: All combustion reactions release energy as heat and light. Burning fuels transfers stored chemical energy to surroundings = Exothermic.

questions.question: When bonds are broken during a chemical reaction, what energy change ALWAYS occurs?
options: Energy is released because atoms move apart naturally
Energy is absorbed to overcome electrostatic attraction
No energy needed since bonds already exist in stable state
Energy fluctuates randomly without consistent pattern
questions.explanation: Breaking bonds ALWAYS requires input of energy (endothermic step). Strong forces between atoms must be overcome by external energy.

questions.question:
During the formation of water from hydrogen and oxygen, new O-H bonds are created in the product.

What happens energetically during bond formation?
options: Energy is absorbed to connect atoms together
Energy is released because stable bonds lower system energy
No net energy once bonds fully form
Energy remains trapped inside newly formed molecules indefinitely
questions.explanation: Bond formation ALWAYS releases energy (exothermic step). Atoms reach more stable lower energy state when connected; excess energy released.

questions.question:
Photosynthesis converts carbon dioxide and water into glucose:

6CO₂ + 6H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂ (requires sunlight)

Why is this classified as endothermic?
options: Plants absorb sunlight providing required energy input
Carbon dioxide naturally loses energy when combining with water
Glucose molecules contain less energy than reactant molecules
Oxygen release indicates energy production rather than consumption
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis requires continuous external energy input from sunlight. Light energy absorbed and stored in chemical bonds of glucose = Endothermic.

questions.question:
In an experiment measuring temperature changes, Student A observes heating while mixing chemicals while Student B observes cooling.

Which combination correctly matches observations with reaction types?
options: A: exothermic, B: endothermic
A: endothermic, B: exothermic
Both observed exothermic reactions
Both observed endothermic reactions
questions.explanation: Heating sensation means energy leaving system to surroundings = exothermic. Cooling sensation means energy entering system from surroundings = endothermic.

questions.question: Identify the correct statement about temperature changes in exothermic reactions.
options: The surroundings get colder because energy enters system
The temperature decreases significantly over time
The surroundings get warmer because energy leaves system
Temperature remains exactly constant throughout
questions.explanation: Exothermic reactions transfer heat outward. Measuring instruments in the immediate environment record a rise in temperature.

questions.question:
Compare two reactions:
Reaction X: Releases energy to surroundings
Reaction Y: Takes in energy from surroundings

Which statement is correct?
options: X is endothermic and Y is exothermic
Both are exothermic
X is exothermic and Y is endothermic
Both are endothermic
questions.explanation: Releasing energy = exothermic. Taking in energy = endothermic. These define opposite energy flow directions relative to system.

questions.question: Which type of reaction would you expect to cause the container to feel hot to touch after mixing?
options: Endothermic dissolution only
Exothermic neutralisation only
Both exothermic and endothermic equally
Neutralisation never affects temperature
questions.explanation: Hot container = energy transferred to surroundings = exothermic reaction. Neutralisation reactions typically release heat.

questions.question: Complete the sentence: In every chemical reaction, energy is _____ to break existing bonds and energy is _____ when new bonds form.
options: absorbed...released
released...absorbed
transferred...stored
created...destroyed
questions.explanation: Fundamental principle: Breaking bonds always absorbs energy (endothermic step). Forming bonds always releases energy (exothermic step).

questions.question:
A student heats calcium carbonate strongly until it decomposes:
CaCO₃(s) → CaO(s) + CO₂(g)
The reaction stops immediately when heating is removed.

What does this indicate?
options: Reaction is exothermic and continues once started
Reaction is endothermic and needs continuous energy supply
Heat acts as catalyst lowering energy requirement
Carbon dioxide produced speeds up reaction rate
questions.explanation: Depends on continuous heat input. When source removed, reaction halts immediately = endothermic requiring constant energy absorption.

questions.question:
Thermal decomposition of metal carbonates generally requires heating:

MgCO₃ + Heat → MgO + CO₂

Why does this make them endothermic processes?
options: Metal oxides are cooler than carbonates naturally
Strong bonds in carbonate require energy input to break
Heat lowers the stability of carbon dioxide product
Metal carbonates absorb moisture from air
questions.explanation: Decomposition requires breaking strong ionic/covalent bonds within carbonate structure. External heat provides necessary energy input = endothermic.

questions.question: Identify the pair of processes where FIRST is endothermic and SECOND is exothermic:
options: Melting ice ... Freezing water
Freezing water ... Melting ice
Condensing steam ... Boiling water
Sublimation ... Condensation
questions.explanation: Melting (solid→liquid) absorbs heat = endothermic. Freezing (liquid→solid) releases heat = exothermic. Same substance phase changes show opposite energy flows.

questions.question:
A reaction releases more energy when forming new bonds than it uses to break old bonds.

How is this reaction classified?
options: Endothermic because some energy was used
Exothermic because net energy was released
Neutral because energy was neither lost nor gained
Impossible under normal conditions
questions.explanation: Net release occurs when forming bonds releases more energy than breaking bonds consumes. Result = Exothermic overall.

questions.question: Why do explosives like TNT release massive amounts of energy upon detonation?
options: TNT contains unstable bonds that break requiring huge energy input
Formation of very stable N₂, H₂O, CO₂ releases far more energy than used to break TNT bonds
Detonation triggers nuclear fission rather than chemical reaction
Slow decomposition produces small amounts continuously
questions.explanation: Explosives produce MORE stable bonds in products than were present in original compound. Large difference in bond energies = massive net energy release.

questions.question:
In the reaction between magnesium ribbon and dilute hydrochloric acid:
Mg(s) + 2HCl(aq) → MgCl₂(aq) + H₂(g)

Temperature rises from 22°C to 35°C.

What energy change occurs?
options: Energy was absorbed from surroundings
Energy was released to surroundings
No energy change occurred
Energy was converted to electrical energy
questions.explanation: Temperature rise indicates energy flowing from system to surroundings = Exothermic reaction. Magnesium reacts vigorously releasing heat.

questions.question: Select the reaction type that ALWAYS releases energy to surroundings.
options: Electrolysis of water
Combustion of fuels
Thermal decomposition
Dissolving most salts in water
questions.explanation: Combustion consistently releases energy. Electrolysis and thermal decomposition require energy input. Dissolution varies by salt type.
